## Radial Timeline 8.0.4

Scene breaks that hold dialogue reach your exported manuscript, and story maps keep their details while Canvas files sync.

### Fixes

- **Manuscript export:** a scene break written as a `---` block keeps every line inside it in your PDF, Word and Markdown exports, including dialogue such as `Kade: Get down!`. Only the frontmatter at the very top of each scene and matter note is left out of the manuscript.
- **Story maps:** a story map keeps its review details while its Canvas file is still arriving from another device through sync, so **Map out of date — review updates** and text drops work as soon as the Canvas lands. Deleting a map's Canvas still removes its stored details.

## Radial Timeline 8.0.3

Drop text onto story maps, privacy updates for shared timelines and Local AI, and fixes.

### New

- **Drop text onto a story map.** Drag a selection from any note onto a subplot lane of a story map, and Radial Timeline creates a scene there. While you drag, the map shows where it will go. The new scene is numbered between its neighbours and gets the lane's subplot and act, and its card joins the map. Drop outside the lanes to make a sketch instead. This works on maps made with Radial Timeline 8.0.2 or later; for an older map, use **Review map details** to create a tracked copy first.
- **Watch the Beat Manager how-to.** A play icon on **Settings → Core → Story beats system** opens a short video on building and fitting a beat system.

### Privacy

- **Shared timelines:** every shared line of text, including scene titles, synopses, acts, status, publish stage and the book's title, subtitle and author, now carries only the words a reader sees. A link to a note shares as its name or alias, a web link as its shown text, and an embedded picture or PDF is left out. Note folders, file names and web addresses stay in your vault.
- **Local AI:** when the Base URL points to a plain http address outside your computer and local network, the setting now shows a note that the connection is unencrypted, so you can switch to an https address or a server on your own network. Local addresses such as localhost and your home network work as before.
- **Community sharing:** if a change to which scene details you share can't be confirmed, Settings checks the website's current choice again before you can change another.

### Fixes

- **Beat Manager:** **Save changes** on a new blank system saves it to your library under its name. Before, switching to another system marked it as unsaved, and its custom hover fields went missing.
- **Community timeline sync** waits, with a message, when two scenes share a scene ID and it can't tell which is the original. Give each copy its own ID and sync again.
- **Timetable Panels** show the portrait of the character you chose. A chosen character without a portrait shows none, instead of another character's.
- **Runtime estimates** count the text between scene-break lines (`---`) again, and leave out code blocks and display math.
- **Remove from timeline** works when your Class field has a different name in your property mapping.
- **Canvas:** if a note or a book's subplot colors can't be read, the other cards keep working, and the colors are tried again.
- **Book Manager:** the active book's outline shows its top edge.

## Radial Timeline 8.0.2

Story map updates, settings search, and fixes.

### New

- **Find Radial Timeline settings from Obsidian's settings search.** Search for a section such as Scene properties, Story beats, PDF fonts or an API key, and the result opens Radial Timeline's settings at that section.
- **Review updates to a story map.** When a subplot map you generated no longer matches the manuscript, its navigation bar shows **Map out of date — review updates**. The review lists new and removed scenes, changed acts and subplots, a changed scene order, and your own edits to the Canvas. **Create updated copy** rebuilds the scene layout in a new Canvas and places your added or edited cards to its right. The original map stays as it is.
- **Bring your cards from an older map.** A map created before this release has no record of its original settings, so the review offers a clean map instead. Select your own cards on the old Canvas first, and they are placed beside the new map.
- **Switch a story map between horizontal and vertical lanes** from its navigation bar, and back.

### Fixes

- **Beat Manager:** **Repair** works for library systems such as Hero's Journey, as well as custom ones. A new blank system can be named before it is saved, and its beat notes use that name.
- **Story maps:** a new map is kept and opened even if its details can't be saved, so trying again no longer makes a duplicate. Deleting a story map's Canvas also removes its stored copy from the plugin's settings.
- **Canvas conversion:** if converting cards stops partway, the notes already created stay linked to their cards, and the notice lists them. A conversion that finished is no longer reported as stopped when the timeline can't open afterward.
- **Sketches:** if a new sketch's position can't be saved, the sketch is kept and the notice says where it is. A failed placement puts the sketches back in their acts.
- **Hover:** hovering the timeline dims the other beat titles so the hovered one stands out. Hovering a Timetable row or Canvas card does the same, and mutes the character ring as a timeline hover does.
- **Story map navigation bar:** the drag bar is wider and keeps its size while you drag.
- **Timetable:** in a narrow pane, the Canvas menu opens under the compact menu instead of the window's corner.
- **Time references:** Escape closes the chooser and returns focus to its marker without reopening it, including in pop-out windows.
- **Image menu:** when a card's chosen place picture has been deleted or renamed, the menu says the picture is missing.
- **Export presets:** applying a preset to a single-file or folder export no longer marks the preset as changed.

## Radial Timeline 8.0.1

New Story Vault editions for Radial Timeline 8.0.

### Story Vaults

- **The Story Vaults use Narration.** Pride & Prejudice, The Odyssey and Sherlock Holmes are repackaged with the 8.0 scene field, so a newly added Story Vault opens without the field-rename alert in Settings.
- **Every book has a Timetable and a subplot map.** Each Story Vault includes a Timetable for each of its books and a Canvas map of its subplots with scene cards.
- **Pride & Prejudice adds pictures of its nine places**, shown with the 29 character portraits in Timetable Panels. Its download is now 20 MB.
- **An earlier Story Vault is offered the new edition.** When you open a vault from an earlier download, the Welcome screen offers the 2026-11-10 edition as a separate download.

### Changes

- **No Pro labels.** Settings, Inquiry, manuscript options and the runtime dialogs no longer mark features as Pro.

## Radial Timeline 8.0.0 Your book on a Canvas, and a Timetable you can plan in: subplot maps that follow the timeline, Panels with character portraits, an Outline layout that turns planning documents into sketches, and scenes you can place by dragging in the table. On the timeline, character lanes follow your main characters. ### Canvas story maps - **Map your subplots on a Canvas.** **Canvas map** in the Timetable or the Canvas icon in the timeline title bar opens an existing map, lets you choose another Canvas, or creates a new subplot map. **Canvas create subplot map** also creates one: choose **Horizontal lanes**, **Vertical lanes**, or a **Single story line**, an act or subplot, and the third of the book to open on. Each card links to its scene note, and lines follow each subplot in reading order. Moving cards does not reorder your manuscript. - **The map and the timeline point at each other.** Hold Shift as you hover a scene on the timeline and its cards light up on the map; with **Follow Shift-hover from timeline in Canvas** on, the map travels to it. Click a card to light its scene on the timeline and in the Timetable. A card's menu adds **Radial Timeline: Show in Timetable**, **Radial Timeline: Show on timeline** and **Radial Timeline: Promote to scene**. - **Find your way around.** The story navigation bar steps scene by scene with a slider (*Scene 16 of 61 · Wickham's Story*), with **Zoom to selection** and **Fit all**. **Canvas card view** shows notes from your books as a **Preview** of the synopsis, the **Title**, or the **Full note**, and can mark overdue scenes. Cards show portraits and places with the same image choices as Timetable Panels, and a picture's focus point crops it alike in both. Other notes keep Obsidian's usual look. Double-click a card to edit its note. - **From a mind map to a timeline in one step.** **Turn Canvas cards into scenes or sketches** makes numbered scenes straight from a Canvas: each card joins its act and its subplot, and the timeline opens. The cards you leave out stay on the map. - **Color cards by subplot.** Right-click idea cards and choose **Radial Timeline: Color by subplot**: the book's subplots in their timeline colors, or **New subplot…** in a free palette color, offered on every Canvas of the book. In the dialog, each card color starts on its subplot, and when you create the scenes every card takes its subplot's timeline color. Radial Timeline remembers the subplot each card was given, so the cards keep it when ring colors move. - **Act cards set the acts.** A card named *Act 2* or *Act 2: The Fall* starts that act, and the cards after it join. With no Act cards, scenes spread evenly across the acts, and the dialog shows where each act starts. - **A key for the map.** The **✱** on the Canvas bar sums up the workflow and the map's marks. - **Turn Canvas ideas into placed sketches.** Choose **Sketches** for loose ideas: **Place after scene**, or **End of act or unassigned**, with **Move up** and **Move down** to set their order. - **Sketches promoted together keep their order.** Each takes a scene number at the end of its act. See [Canvas story maps](https://github.com/EricRhysTaylor/radial-timeline/wiki/Timetable#canvas-story-maps). ### Timetable - **Panels.** A card for every scene, beat and sketch, with its date, rings, characters and synopsis beside an image: a character's portrait, the place, both side by side, the portrait over a place background, or none. **Character selection** picks whose portrait: the most distinctive character in the scene, the first or second listed, the POV character, or a balanced variety. Pictures belong to people and places: each comes from the `Image` on the character or Place note, or else a picture named after it, so an image called *Elizabeth Bennet* shows up for Elizabeth Bennet. A card's picture button says where its portrait and place come from, and **Choose portrait…** or **Choose place image…** changes them for that card. **Place background + character** sets the portrait over the place, with a **Text backing** that keeps the card readable, and **Portrait shape** is Square or Landscape. In a narrow pane, every image choice sits in one **Image settings** menu. **Image sizing** fills or fits, **Set image focus** keeps the right part in view, and **Panel size** is Small, Medium or Large. Click a synopsis to edit it in place. - **Outline.** The book act by act in reading order, with **Outline documents** on top: notes with `Class: Outline` appear there by themselves, and you can attach any other note. Select text in a document and **Add selection as sketch** puts it where you clicked in the outline. **Create sketches from this document** turns a document's headings into sketches you review first; each links back to its source, and the document stays as it is. - **Quick Workspace** opens a reference document next to the table: side by side, below, or with the timeline as well, with your pinned tabs kept open. **Timetable above Canvas** puts your book's subplot map under the table. - **Add any note to the book by dragging it in.** Drag a note from the file explorer onto the Timetable or the timeline, choose **Scene** or **Sketch**, and it joins the book with its text and properties intact. In Narrative or Progress, drop it on a scene on the timeline and it becomes the next scene, in that scene's act and the subplot you dropped it on. With no book set up yet, **Create book** in the dialog makes your first one and carries on with the note. - **Drop text to make a sketch.** Drag a selection from any note onto the timeline or Timetable, and **Create sketch** keeps a link back to its source. In Outline, drop it on a row and the sketch lands right there. - **Place scenes and sketches from the table.** Drag a scene's grip onto another scene to place it just before it, with no timeline open. In Narrative this reorders the manuscript; in Chronologue it places the scene in time. Sketches drag to sit after a scene, beside another sketch, or at the end of an act, and empty acts accept drops. When a scene with sketches after it moves to another act, **Move attached sketches?** asks whether they follow it. - **Sketch notes hold only your writing.** Where each sketch sits among the scenes lives in `Radial Timeline/Sketch Placement/placements.json`, which syncs with your vault and follows a sketch when you rename or move it. A sketch keeps its `Source` link to the outline it came from. Sketches you placed in an earlier version keep their place: their `Place after scene` and `Sketch order` lines are copied over once, and stay in your notes for you to keep or delete. - **A toolbar of its own.** Switch the layout between **Table**, **Panels** and **Outline**, switch books, and pin a mode from the **Mode** menu; a lock marks a pinned mode. **Restore Radial Timetable view**, beside **Saved views**, adds a fresh view if yours was deleted. New Timetables name their views **Radial Timetable** and **Spreadsheet**. - **The timeline lights rows without moving the table.** Hover a scene on the timeline and its row lights in Table, Panels and Outline; hold Shift as you hover to bring the row into view, as Canvas does with its cards. A pointer or a dragged file crossing the timeline leaves the table where it is. - **Promote into place.** A sketch placed after a scene is promoted into that spot with a number that fits between its neighbors, and **Open scene** takes you to it. - **Color by a column in one click, and search from the key.** Right-click a column header and the timeline takes its colors at once; **Edit key** chooses others. Buttons in the key set how the names you pick combine: **Both present**, **Either present**, **Neither present** or **Alone together**, and **With** or **Without** for one name. A scene takes the color of its rarest name, so a character in nearly every scene leaves room for the others. The key is see-through and spans the timeline's pane, so the top of the timeline stays in view. - **Due coloring keeps up with the calendar.** Color a Timetable by **Due** or a date range and every group colors as scenes reach it: a scene that turns Overdue or due Today takes that group's color on the timeline and in the key, and each group keeps its own color. **Edit key** lists every group, empty ones included. Coloring by day, month, or year shows the eight busiest periods, or the ones you pick. Views you colored by date in 7.7.0 color every group again; choose groups in **Edit key** to narrow them. - **Promote lists each scene once, in reading order.** When you promote a sketch, its **Position** menu offers every scene of the book once, from the first scene to the last. - **Commands are grouped by what they act on.** Each name starts with what it works on, so related commands sit together in the Command Palette: **Timeline open**, **Inquiry open**, **Note create**, **Manuscript import**, **Timetable open**, **Timetable reset columns to recommended**, **Timetable restore a Radial Timetable view**, **Scene promote note**, **Canvas create subplot map**, **Canvas convert cards to scenes or sketches**, and **Community timeline share export**. Hotkeys you set keep working. See [Timetable](https://github.com/EricRhysTaylor/radial-timeline/wiki/Timetable). ### Timeline - **Each book sets its own narration.** Open a book's details, the tag button on its card in **Settings → Core → Books**, and choose first person, second person, third person, omniscient or objective. The synopsis marks each scene's POV character, the first name in `Character`, by its own book's narration, so a saga can hold a first-person novel beside an omniscient one. Your earlier vault-wide choice becomes every book's narration, so your timeline looks just as it did. - **Narration marks a scene that departs from its book.** `Narration: first` marks a letter inside a third-person novel, and `Narration: two` a scene two characters carry. New scenes carry the field empty, and a scene that follows its book leaves it that way. - **Bring your POV fields across in one step.** **Scene field POV is now Narration**, at the top of **Settings → Core**, renames `POV` to `Narration` in every scene and keeps each value exactly as you wrote it. Where a scene already has a `Narration` value, a `POV` that says something else stays beside it, listed with a link to its scene for you to review. New scenes get an empty `Narration` property, ready for the scenes narrated differently from their book. Until you apply it, Radial Timeline reads `POV` just as before. Afterward, the scene properties check lists each scene whose `Narration` holds a character's name, with its value, so you can give it a narration such as `first` or `two`, or clear it to follow the book. - **Character lanes in Narrative mode.** Turn them on with the eye button in the ring key, or **Settings → Core → Narration → Character lanes**, to follow your main characters through the book. Up to four thin lanes sit inside the outer ring, one for each of the characters who are POV in the most scenes. Each lane has its own color. A tall mark is a scene told from their point of view; a short mark is a scene they're in. Gaps show how long a character is gone. Hover a mark to outline it, light its scene and show the character's name right beside it. The ring key (layers icon, or hold Shift) lists the lanes below the rings, each name beside its color, and, while open, shows the names on the timeline too; hovering a name lights every scene that character is in. - **Time references read at a glance.** In Chronologue, each date mark is an arrowhead pointing the way its date lies from the scene, a double arrowhead for dates before or after the timeline, and a diamond for both ways. Lines draw in your theme's text color, so they read over every subplot. Hover a scene's source circle to see all of its references at once, listed beside the timeline, and opening one scrolls the note to its passage. - **Dates before the common era.** Write `BCE` after a scene's `When`, as in `When: 1184-06-14 BCE` or `When: 44 BCE`. Chronologue, the hover, the scene time bar and the Timetable count the years down to 1 BCE and name the era: *1184 BCE*. A book that runs on into the common era names *CE* on its later years. - **The rotate toggle is gone.** The timeline opens with Act 1 at 12 o'clock. - **New vaults renumber scene files after a drag.** **Manuscript ripple rename** in **Settings → Advanced** starts on, so scene file numbers follow the order you drag scenes into. A vault that already has the setting keeps it. - **A new book opens on an empty timeline.** **Open Timetable** leads to the Outline, where an outline document starts the book. The Welcome screen closes from its corner. - **Help in the title bar.** **Help** sits with the title-bar actions, and **Settings** opens from the gear. - **Stage milestones live in Settings.** **Settings → Core → Progress and status** marks each stage you finish, and the timeline stays clear for your book. See [Character lanes](https://github.com/EricRhysTaylor/radial-timeline/wiki/Narrative-Mode#character-lanes) and [Time references](https://github.com/EricRhysTaylor/radial-timeline/wiki/Time-References#read-the-timeline). ### Inquiry - **Read a briefing beside Inquiry.** The **Open beside Inquiry** icon in a Briefing Article moves it into a side panel next to Inquiry, so you can read its findings while you work through the book. **Open full briefing** brings it back to the full-size view. ### Manuscript export - **Highlights print as plain text.** PDF and Word exports keep your highlighted words and leave out the `==` marks and any color. Markdown exports keep them as you wrote them. - **A saved range keeps up with the book.** A scene range that runs to the last scene now stays open-ended, so scenes you add later are included in the next export. A range that stops earlier is kept as you set it. ### Writing Session - **A formatting key on every note.** The signature icon at the far right of a note's title bar lists Obsidian's formatting, with each one's hotkey and what to type. Select some words and click: bold, italic, highlights in color, headings, lists, footnotes, tables and all thirteen callouts go in around your selection. It opens in the right gutter when you hover it and leaves with the pointer. Click the icon to keep it open; Esc, a click elsewhere or a second click puts it away. - **Desk Lamps help.** A **?** beside Desk Lamps in the session panel explains that lamps share live sessions with the friends you choose, at any sharing level, Private included. The line under the checkboxes says what ticked friends see. - **Give each scene its share of a session.** Saving a session can split its minutes and words across the scenes you worked on, and add that time to each scene's **Total Time**. **Total Time** is now a core scene property, so the audit lists it on your existing scenes and **Insert missing fields** adds it. ### Story Vaults - **Story Vaults live under Settings → Resources.** The **Res** tab replaces the Pro tab: the Story Vaults, then **Learn more** links to Getting started, the wiki and the video tutorials. - **Story Vaults know their edition.** When a newer edition of a story is ready, the Welcome screen and **Settings → Resources** offer it as a separate download, and your current vault stays as it is. - **Story Vaults open with their narration set.** Pride & Prejudice is narrated in the third person, the Sherlock Holmes novels in the first person, and The Odyssey by an omniscient narrator, each set in its book details. - **Portraits and places in Pride & Prejudice.** The next Pride & Prejudice Story Vault edition includes 29 storybook character portraits, nine place images, a Timetable and a subplot map. Open the Timetable in **Panels** to see the images alongside the scenes. ### Community - **Share your timeline from Settings.** Turn on **Share timeline** in **Settings → Community** and the book's timeline arrives on your Community account, private until you review it. **Open preview** opens the Complete Preview, where you reveal scenes, and a live timeline keeps up with your book sync. - **See your Community sync in the Mailbox.** A row in the Mailbox shows when your book list last reached My Share and when the next sync runs; click it to sync now. An open vault refreshes the list every six hours. ### AI - **AI off keeps your work in your vault.** Turning AI off closes every connection to AI providers and local servers, and saved Pulse grades still color the scene numbers. - **AI content logs are off in new vaults by default.** Turn on **Enable AI content logs** in **Settings → Advanced** to keep prompts, submitted material and responses in your vault's log files. A vault that already logs keeps its setting. - **Gemini API requests opt out of Google's request storage.** Radial Timeline sends every request to the Gemini API with `store: false`. Google turned request storage on by default for new paid API projects on October 26; your manuscript text stays out of it. ### Fixes - **A portable Timetable opens again.** When a book already has a matching Radial Timetable in `Radial Timeline/Timetables`, a fresh installation opens it instead of offering to create a duplicate. - **Story Vaults keep their narration and maps.** Opening a recognized Story Vault sets the narration defaults for its new book profiles. Adding a story to an existing vault keeps its packaged Timetables and Canvas maps connected to the imported books. - **No more `{{Character}}` in your scenes.** **Insert missing fields** and **Fill empty values** add empty fields instead of copying the template's placeholders, such as `{{Character}}` or `{{When}}`, into a scene.

Views you colored by date in 7.7.0 color every group again; choose groups in **Edit key** to narrow them. - **Promote lists each scene once, in reading order.** When you promote a sketch, its **Position** menu offers every scene of the book once, from the first scene to the last. - **Commands are grouped by what they act on.** Each name starts with what it works on, so related commands sit together in the Command Palette: **Timeline open**, **Inquiry open**, **Note create**, **Manuscript import**, **Timetable open**, **Timetable reset columns to recommended**, **Timetable restore a Radial Timetable view**, **Scene promote note**, **Canvas create subplot map**, **Canvas convert cards to scenes or sketches**, and **Community timeline share export**. Hotkeys you set keep working. See [Timetable](https://github.com/EricRhysTaylor/radial-timeline/wiki/Timetable). ### Timeline - **Each book sets its own narration.** Open a book's details, the tag button on its card in **Settings → Core → Books**, and choose first person, second person, third person, omniscient or objective. The synopsis marks each scene's POV character, the first name in `Character`, by its own book's narration, so a saga can hold a first-person novel beside an omniscient one. Your earlier vault-wide choice becomes every book's narration, so your timeline looks just as it did. - **Narration marks a scene that departs from its book.** `Narration: first` marks a letter inside a third-person novel, and `Narration: two` a scene two characters carry. New scenes carry the field empty, and a scene that follows its book leaves it that way. - **Bring your POV fields across in one step.** **Scene field POV is now Narration**, at the top of **Settings → Core**, renames `POV` to `Narration` in every scene and keeps each value exactly as you wrote it. Where a scene already has a `Narration` value, a `POV` that says something else stays beside it, listed with a link to its scene for you to review. New scenes get an empty `Narration` property, ready for the scenes narrated differently from their book. Until you apply it, Radial Timeline reads `POV` just as before. Afterward, the scene properties check lists each scene whose `Narration` holds a character's name, with its value, so you can give it a narration such as `first` or `two`, or clear it to follow the book. - **Character lanes in Narrative mode.** Turn them on with the eye button in the ring key, or **Settings → Core → Narration → Character lanes**, to follow your main characters through the book. Up to four thin lanes sit inside the outer ring, one for each of the characters who are POV in the most scenes. Each lane has its own color. A tall mark is a scene told from their point of view; a short mark is a scene they're in. Gaps show how long a character is gone. Hover a mark to outline it, light its scene and show the character's name right beside it. The ring key (layers icon, or hold Shift) lists the lanes below the rings, each name beside its color, and, while open, shows the names on the timeline too; hovering a name lights every scene that character is in. - **Time references read at a glance.** In Chronologue, each date mark is an arrowhead pointing the way its date lies from the scene, a double arrowhead for dates before or after the timeline, and a diamond for both ways. Lines draw in your theme's text color, so they read over every subplot. Hover a scene's source circle to see all of its references at once, listed beside the timeline, and opening one scrolls the note to its passage. - **Dates before the common era.** Write `BCE` after a scene's `When`, as in `When: 1184-06-14 BCE` or `When: 44 BCE`. Chronologue, the hover, the scene time bar and the Timetable count the years down to 1 BCE and name the era: *1184 BCE*. A book that runs on into the common era names *CE* on its later years. - **The rotate toggle is gone.** The timeline opens with Act 1 at 12 o'clock. - **New vaults renumber scene files after a drag.** **Manuscript ripple rename** in **Settings → Advanced** starts on, so scene file numbers follow the order you drag scenes into. A vault that already has the setting keeps it. - **A new book opens on an empty timeline.** **Open Timetable** leads to the Outline, where an outline document starts the book. The Welcome screen closes from its corner. - **Help in the title bar.** **Help** sits with the title-bar actions, and **Settings** opens from the gear. - **Stage milestones live in Settings.** **Settings → Core → Progress and status** marks each stage you finish, and the timeline stays clear for your book. See [Character lanes](https://github.com/EricRhysTaylor/radial-timeline/wiki/Narrative-Mode#character-lanes) and [Time references](https://github.com/EricRhysTaylor/radial-timeline/wiki/Time-References#read-the-timeline). ### Inquiry - **Read a briefing beside Inquiry.** The **Open beside Inquiry** icon in a Briefing Article moves it into a side panel next to Inquiry, so you can read its findings while you work through the book. **Open full briefing** brings it back to the full-size view. ### Manuscript export - **Highlights print as plain text.** PDF and Word exports keep your highlighted words and leave out the `==` marks and any color. Markdown exports keep them as you wrote them. - **A saved range keeps up with the book.** A scene range that runs to the last scene now stays open-ended, so scenes you add later are included in the next export. A range that stops earlier is kept as you set it. ### Writing Session - **A formatting key on every note.** The signature icon at the far right of a note's title bar lists Obsidian's formatting, with each one's hotkey and what to type. Select some words and click: bold, italic, highlights in color, headings, lists, footnotes, tables and all thirteen callouts go in around your selection. It opens in the right gutter when you hover it and leaves with the pointer. Click the icon to keep it open; Esc, a click elsewhere or a second click puts it away. - **Desk Lamps help.** A **?** beside Desk Lamps in the session panel explains that lamps share live sessions with the friends you choose, at any sharing level, Private included. The line under the checkboxes says what ticked friends see. - **Give each scene its share of a session.** Saving a session can split its minutes and words across the scenes you worked on, and add that time to each scene's **Total Time**. **Total Time** is now a core scene property, so the audit lists it on your existing scenes and **Insert missing fields** adds it. ### Story Vaults - **Story Vaults live under Settings → Resources.** The **Res** tab replaces the Pro tab: the Story Vaults, then **Learn more** links to Getting started, the wiki and the video tutorials. - **Story Vaults know their edition.** When a newer edition of a story is ready, the Welcome screen and **Settings → Resources** offer it as a separate download, and your current vault stays as it is. - **Story Vaults open with their narration set.** Pride & Prejudice is narrated in the third person, the Sherlock Holmes novels in the first person, and The Odyssey by an omniscient narrator, each set in its book details. - **Portraits and places in Pride & Prejudice.** The next Pride & Prejudice Story Vault edition includes 29 storybook character portraits, nine place images, a Timetable and a subplot map. Open the Timetable in **Panels** to see the images alongside the scenes. ### Community - **Share your timeline from Settings.** Turn on **Share timeline** in **Settings → Community** and the book's timeline arrives on your Community account, private until you review it. **Open preview** opens the Complete Preview, where you reveal scenes, and a live timeline keeps up with your book sync. - **See your Community sync in the Mailbox.** A row in the Mailbox shows when your book list last reached My Share and when the next sync runs; click it to sync now. An open vault refreshes the list every six hours. ### AI - **AI off keeps your work in your vault.** Turning AI off closes every connection to AI providers and local servers, and saved Pulse grades still color the scene numbers. - **AI content logs are off in new vaults by default.** Turn on **Enable AI content logs** in **Settings → Advanced** to keep prompts, submitted material and responses in your vault's log files. A vault that already logs keeps its setting. - **Gemini API requests opt out of Google's request storage.** Radial Timeline sends every request to the Gemini API with `store: false`. Google turned request storage on by default for new paid API projects on October 26; your manuscript text stays out of it. ### Fixes - **A portable Timetable opens again.** When a book already has a matching Radial Timetable in `Radial Timeline/Timetables`, a fresh installation opens it instead of offering to create a duplicate. - **Story Vaults keep their narration and maps.** Opening a recognized Story Vault sets the narration defaults for its new book profiles. Adding a story to an existing vault keeps its packaged Timetables and Canvas maps connected to the imported books. - **No more `{{Character}}` in your scenes.** **Insert missing fields** and **Fill empty values** add empty fields instead of copying the template's placeholders, such as `{{Character}}` or `{{When}}`, into a scene.

## Radial Timeline 8.0.4

Scene breaks that hold dialogue reach your exported manuscript, and story maps keep their details while Canvas files sync.

### Fixes

- **Manuscript export:** a scene break written as a `---` block keeps every line inside it in your PDF, Word and Markdown exports, including dialogue such as `Kade: Get down!`. Only the frontmatter at the very top of each scene and matter note is left out of the manuscript.
- **Story maps:** a story map keeps its review details while its Canvas file is still arriving from another device through sync, so **Map out of date — review updates** and text drops work as soon as the Canvas lands. Deleting a map's Canvas still removes its stored details.

## Radial Timeline 8.0.3

Drop text onto story maps, privacy updates for shared timelines and Local AI, and fixes.

### New

- **Drop text onto a story map.** Drag a selection from any note onto a subplot lane of a story map, and Radial Timeline creates a scene there. While you drag, the map shows where it will go. The new scene is numbered between its neighbours and gets the lane's subplot and act, and its card joins the map. Drop outside the lanes to make a sketch instead. This works on maps made with Radial Timeline 8.0.2 or later; for an older map, use **Review map details** to create a tracked copy first.
- **Watch the Beat Manager how-to.** A play icon on **Settings → Core → Story beats system** opens a short video on building and fitting a beat system.

### Privacy

- **Shared timelines:** every shared line of text, including scene titles, synopses, acts, status, publish stage and the book's title, subtitle and author, now carries only the words a reader sees. A link to a note shares as its name or alias, a web link as its shown text, and an embedded picture or PDF is left out. Note folders, file names and web addresses stay in your vault.
- **Local AI:** when the Base URL points to a plain http address outside your computer and local network, the setting now shows a note that the connection is unencrypted, so you can switch to an https address or a server on your own network. Local addresses such as localhost and your home network work as before.
- **Community sharing:** if a change to which scene details you share can't be confirmed, Settings checks the website's current choice again before you can change another.

### Fixes

- **Beat Manager:** **Save changes** on a new blank system saves it to your library under its name. Before, switching to another system marked it as unsaved, and its custom hover fields went missing.
- **Community timeline sync** waits, with a message, when two scenes share a scene ID and it can't tell which is the original. Give each copy its own ID and sync again.
- **Timetable Panels** show the portrait of the character you chose. A chosen character without a portrait shows none, instead of another character's.
- **Runtime estimates** count the text between scene-break lines (`---`) again, and leave out code blocks and display math.
- **Remove from timeline** works when your Class field has a different name in your property mapping.
- **Canvas:** if a note or a book's subplot colors can't be read, the other cards keep working, and the colors are tried again.
- **Book Manager:** the active book's outline shows its top edge.

## Radial Timeline 8.0.2

Story map updates, settings search, and fixes.

### New

- **Find Radial Timeline settings from Obsidian's settings search.** Search for a section such as Scene properties, Story beats, PDF fonts or an API key, and the result opens Radial Timeline's settings at that section.
- **Review updates to a story map.** When a subplot map you generated no longer matches the manuscript, its navigation bar shows **Map out of date — review updates**. The review lists new and removed scenes, changed acts and subplots, a changed scene order, and your own edits to the Canvas. **Create updated copy** rebuilds the scene layout in a new Canvas and places your added or edited cards to its right. The original map stays as it is.
- **Bring your cards from an older map.** A map created before this release has no record of its original settings, so the review offers a clean map instead. Select your own cards on the old Canvas first, and they are placed beside the new map.
- **Switch a story map between horizontal and vertical lanes** from its navigation bar, and back.

### Fixes

- **Beat Manager:** **Repair** works for library systems such as Hero's Journey, as well as custom ones. A new blank system can be named before it is saved, and its beat notes use that name.
- **Story maps:** a new map is kept and opened even if its details can't be saved, so trying again no longer makes a duplicate. Deleting a story map's Canvas also removes its stored copy from the plugin's settings.
- **Canvas conversion:** if converting cards stops partway, the notes already created stay linked to their cards, and the notice lists them. A conversion that finished is no longer reported as stopped when the timeline can't open afterward.
- **Sketches:** if a new sketch's position can't be saved, the sketch is kept and the notice says where it is. A failed placement puts the sketches back in their acts.
- **Hover:** hovering the timeline dims the other beat titles so the hovered one stands out. Hovering a Timetable row or Canvas card does the same, and mutes the character ring as a timeline hover does.
- **Story map navigation bar:** the drag bar is wider and keeps its size while you drag.
- **Timetable:** in a narrow pane, the Canvas menu opens under the compact menu instead of the window's corner.
- **Time references:** Escape closes the chooser and returns focus to its marker without reopening it, including in pop-out windows.
- **Image menu:** when a card's chosen place picture has been deleted or renamed, the menu says the picture is missing.
- **Export presets:** applying a preset to a single-file or folder export no longer marks the preset as changed.

## Radial Timeline 8.0.1

New Story Vault editions for Radial Timeline 8.0.

### Story Vaults

- **The Story Vaults use Narration.** Pride & Prejudice, The Odyssey and Sherlock Holmes are repackaged with the 8.0 scene field, so a newly added Story Vault opens without the field-rename alert in Settings.
- **Every book has a Timetable and a subplot map.** Each Story Vault includes a Timetable for each of its books and a Canvas map of its subplots with scene cards.
- **Pride & Prejudice adds pictures of its nine places**, shown with the 29 character portraits in Timetable Panels. Its download is now 20 MB.
- **An earlier Story Vault is offered the new edition.** When you open a vault from an earlier download, the Welcome screen offers the 2026-11-10 edition as a separate download.

### Changes

- **No Pro labels.** Settings, Inquiry, manuscript options and the runtime dialogs no longer mark features as Pro.
